title: Grade 10 Science — Light & Heredity and Evolution
description: Light — Reflection and Refraction and Heredity and Evolution practice questions
subject: science

questions.question: The image formed in a plane mirror is:
questions.explanation: A plane mirror always forms a virtual (cannot be projected on a screen), erect image at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.question: A concave mirror is used in torches and car headlights because it:
options: Converges parallel rays to the focus
questions.explanation: When a light source is placed at the focus of a concave mirror, the reflected rays become parallel — producing a strong, parallel beam of light ideal for torches.

questions.question: If the speed of light in glass is 2 × 10⁸ m/s, the refractive index of glass is:
questions.explanation: n = speed of light in vacuum / speed of light in medium = (3 × 10⁸) / (2 × 10⁸) = 1.5.

questions.question: A concave lens always forms an image that is:
questions.explanation: A concave (diverging) lens always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image regardless of the position of the object.

questions.question: An object is placed 20 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The image distance is:
questions.explanation: Using mirror formula with sign convention (distances measured from pole, real distances negative for concave): 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. u = −20, f = −10. 1/v = 1/(−10) − 1/(−20) = −1/10 + 1/20 = −1/20. v = −20 cm.

questions.question: The power of a convex lens with focal length 50 cm is:
questions.explanation: P = 1/f (in metres) = 1/0.5 = +2 D. Convex lenses have positive power because they converge light.

questions.question: When a ray of light goes from a denser medium to a rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle, the phenomenon is called:
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle. No refraction occurs — all light is reflected back.

questions.question: The dispersion of white light in a glass prism occurs because different colours of light have different:
questions.explanation: Different colours have different wavelengths, and each wavelength has a slightly different refractive index in glass. Violet light bends most, red least — causing dispersion into a spectrum.

questions.question: The scientific study of heredity and variation is called:
questions.explanation: Genetics is the branch of biology that deals with heredity (how traits pass from parents to offspring) and variation (differences between individuals).

questions.question: DNA stands for:
questions.explanation: DNA — Deoxyribonucleic acid — is the molecule that carries genetic information. It is present in the nucleus of cells and is the basis of heredity.

questions.question: Mendel's Law of Segregation states that:
options: Genes assort independently during gamete formation
Two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation so each gamete has one allele
Dominant traits always suppress recessive traits
questions.explanation: The Law of Segregation: each organism carries two alleles for every trait, and these alleles separate during gamete (sex cell) formation so each gamete receives exactly one allele.

questions.question: When two tall pea plants of genotype Tt are crossed, the probability of getting tall offspring is:
questions.explanation: Tt × Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt, tt in ratio 3:1. Three out of four offspring (TT and Tt) will be tall (T is dominant). So probability = 3/4 = 75%.

questions.question: Homologous organs (like the forelimbs of a bat and a whale) suggest:
questions.explanation: Homologous organs have the same fundamental structure but serve different functions, indicating divergent evolution from a common ancestor. This is evidence for shared evolutionary history.

questions.question: The theory of natural selection (survival of the fittest) was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of natural selection in 'On the Origin of Species' (1859). Organisms best adapted to their environment survive and reproduce more successfully.

questions.question: Vestigial organs in humans (such as the coccyx) serve as evidence of:
options: Evolution from ancestors who used these organs
questions.explanation: Vestigial organs are remnants of structures that were functional in ancestors but are now reduced or non-functional. They provide strong evidence for evolution and a shared ancestral past.
